checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot only serve sidecars for validated blocks?

audit_items.state_context: validateDataColumnsByRootRequest only checks total count <= MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars. Does NOT validate column index values or detect duplicate (root, index) pairs. Storage returns pre-verified VerifiedRODataColumn objects. Rate limiter uses len(columns) including duplicates.

phase1.summary: The handler serves data columns from dataColumnStorage which holds VerifiedRODataColumn objects - columns that already passed the verification pipeline. validateDataColumnsByRootRequest only sums total column count across all identifiers and rejects if the sum exceeds MaxRequestDataColumnSidecars. No validation of column index values for validity (must be in [0, NumberOfColumns)) and no detection of duplicate block roots or duplicate (root, index) pairs within a single request.
state_anomalies: No deduplication of (blockRoot, columnIndex) pairs - a peer can craft a request where the same column is requested twice under different identifiers, potentially causing the same sidecar to be sent twice
No validation that column indices within each ident.Columns are within [0, NumberOfColumns-1]. Out-of-range indices pass the count check and are forwarded to storage
No validation that column indices within a single identifier are unique - Columns=[0,0,0] counts as 3 in the total but all resolve to same sidecar
phase1.cache_analysis: Storage returns pre-verified objects; no cache inconsistency. Storage pruning (minEpochsForDataColumnSidecarsRequest window) is handled gracefully by simply omitting those sidecars with no error, which is spec-compliant.
phase1.concurrency_analysis: Handler does not hold locks during stream; concurrent reconstruction can save new sidecars while streaming is in progress, which is harmless since storage.Get calls are independent.

phase2.summary: Primary concrete exploit: attacker constructs a single DataColumnsByRootIdentifiers request with one identifier entry containing Columns=[0,0,0,...,0] repeated N times up to the limit. The count check sums len(id.Columns)=N, limit is satisfied. Out-of-range index scenario: an index value of uint64(math.MaxUint64) passes the count check and is forwarded to storage - behavior depends on whether storage handles out-of-range indices gracefully.
phase2.counterexample: Partial - duplicate index scenario: validateDataColumnsByRootRequest validates total column count but NOT that column index values are within [0, NumberOfColumns-1]. Out-of-range indices would pass the count check.
attack_scenarios: Duplicate column indices within one identifier: pass the count check, get the same sidecar multiple times (if storage doesn't deduplicate), amplifying server I/O
Out-of-range column indices (e.g., index >= 128): no validation rejects these; storage must handle gracefully

phase2_5.reachability: Handler registered on p2p.RPCDataColumnSidecarsByRootTopicV1 and invoked for any peer-initiated RPC request. Any network peer can send this message after the Fulu fork is active. The only prerequisite is a libp2p connection.
entry_points: P2P RPC stream from any connected peer
phase2_5.classification: exploitable (for duplicate-index and out-of-range-index issues); defense-in-depth (rate limiter provides some protection)

phase3.summary: Intended invariant: 'only serve valid, verified columns within spec limits.' The guard validateDataColumnsByRootRequest only enforces the count upper bound, which is necessary but not sufficient. The Fulu spec for DataColumnSidecarsByRoot requires that column indices be valid (< NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS). This validation is absent.
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Insufficient. Missing: column index range validation, duplicate detection within a request.
edge_cases: Multiple identifiers for the same block root requesting the same column index multiple times

phase3_5.reason: Missing column index range validation is a deviation from the Fulu spec requirement that column indices be valid. While storage may handle out-of-range indices gracefully, this represents an unvalidated trust boundary on an externally-facing RPC endpoint. The duplicate-index issue can cause extra I/O per request without triggering the rate limit properly.
phase3_5.recommendation: Add validation in validateDataColumnsByRootRequest to check that every column index in every identifier satisfies index < NumberOfColumns, and detect/reject duplicate (root, index) pairs within a request.
phase3_5.severity_estimate: Low - practical impact is limited because storage errors are handled gracefully and rate limiter partially mitigates abuse, but represents a spec compliance gap on an external-facing interface

audit_items.final_reasoning: The guard validateDataColumnsByRootRequest only enforces the request size limit but not column index validity. While storage handles out-of-range indices gracefully and the practical exploitability is limited by the rate limiter, this is a spec compliance gap on an externally-facing RPC endpoint. Not a confirmed high-severity vulnerability but worth flagging.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Are blobs from engine_getBlobsV2 correctly handled with trust assumption?

audit_items.state_context: blocks.NewVerifiedRODataColumn documentation: 'should only be used by the verification package'. Called here in the execution package without any KZG proof verification on EL-provided data. Once wrapped as VerifiedRODataColumn, sidecars are stored in dataColumnStorage and broadcast to P2P peers.

phase1.summary: ReconstructDataColumnSidecars fetches blobs and cell proofs from the execution layer (EL) via GetBlobsV2, constructs data column sidecars via peerdas.ConstructDataColumnSidecars, then calls blocks.NewVerifiedRODataColumn - marking each result as cryptographically verified without performing any KZG proof or commitment verification on the EL-provided data. The comment 'We trust the execution layer we are connected to' explicitly documents this intentional design decision.
state_anomalies: EL-provided blobs and cell proofs are used to construct VerifiedRODataColumn objects with no cryptographic verification - if the EL is compromised or returns incorrect data, the resulting objects are stored and broadcast as if fully verified
blobsAndProofs.KzgProofs slice is appended to cellProofs with no check that the number of proofs matches the expected count (NumberOfColumns * blobCount)
Only a nil check on blobsAndProofs is performed, not a nil check on blobsAndProofs.Blob or blobsAndProofs.KzgProofs individually
If EL returns blobs for wrong commitments (valid format but wrong content), ConstructDataColumnSidecars produces sidecars with incorrect data, stored and broadcast as verified
blocks.NewVerifiedRODataColumn is documented as 'should only be used by the verification package' - this invariant is violated
phase1.cache_analysis: Resulting VerifiedRODataColumn objects are stored in dataColumnStorage. Once stored, they are served to peers via RPC and re-broadcast. Malicious or corrupted EL data would persist and spread.
phase1.concurrency_analysis: No lock prevents concurrent calls for the same block root. Double-execution is unlikely to cause issues since results are idempotent, but concurrent EL calls could occur.

phase2.summary: The exploit path: a node operator runs a compromised or buggy EL. The EL returns engine_getBlobsV2 with blobs that have valid format but incorrect content. ReconstructDataColumnSidecars will call peerdas.ConstructDataColumnSidecars with these blobs and proofs. That function constructs data columns but does NOT call verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs. The function returns sidecars wrapped as VerifiedRODataColumn. These sidecars are then: (a) stored in dataColumnStorage, (b) broadcast to P2P peers. Peers receiving via gossip will run full validation including KZG proof verification and reject them. Peers receiving via RPC will trust the serving node.
phase2.counterexample: Yes - a compromised EL is the concrete counterexample. Subtler: even an honest EL with a software bug in engine_getBlobsV2 can return blobs for the wrong versioned hashes (e.g., returning all zeros for missing blobs). These zero-blobs would pass the nil check but produce incorrect data columns.
attack_scenarios: Compromised EL operator injects malicious blobs - beacon node stores and distributes malformed data columns as 'verified'
EL bug returns partial/empty blobs for some commitments but not nil (returns empty byte slice instead) - column construction may produce garbage but not error
EL response with wrong number of KZG proofs - cellProofs count mismatch - ConstructDataColumnSidecars may fail or produce wrong output
phase2.timing_dependencies: None - triggered synchronously when a block arrives via gossip

phase2_5.reachability: This code executes when a new block arrives via block-syncing or gossip. The EL is trusted by design. An external attacker cannot directly trigger GetBlobsV2 responses, but a malicious EL operator (or a MITM on the EL connection if using HTTP) could exploit this. The practical attack surface is limited to the trust boundary between the beacon node and its configured EL.
entry_points: Block arrival via gossip or sync -> onBlock -> subscribeToBlockNotifications -> ReconstructDataColumnSidecars
phase2_5.classification: internal-only / design-level. A full chain attack from external network to this code path is not direct. A compromised EL can corrupt data silently.

phase3.summary: The invariant 'VerifiedRODataColumn represents a cryptographically verified data column' is broken by this code. The NewVerifiedRODataColumn function carries the comment 'should only be used by the verification package,' yet it is called in the execution package without performing any of the required verifications (ValidFields, SidecarKzgProofVerified, SidecarInclusionProven). The design rationale ('we trust the EL') is explicit and intentional but creates a systemic gap: if the EL is ever compromised, malformed data propagates to storage and peers without any cryptographic safety net at the beacon node level.
phase3.guard_identified: blobsAndProofs == nil check and peerdas.ConstructDataColumnSidecars structural validation
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Insufficient for the invariant claimed by VerifiedRODataColumn. The type implies cryptographic verification that is not performed.
edge_cases: EL returns blobs with correct length but incorrect data (not detectable without KZG verification)
EL returns wrong number of proofs per blob
EL returns blobs with valid format but for different block than requested

phase3_5.reason: The explicit bypass of KZG verification on EL-provided data, combined with the misuse of the VerifiedRODataColumn type (documented as 'should only be used by the verification package'), constitutes a design-level trust assumption that could allow a compromised EL to silently inject malformed data columns into the network. Even though this is 'by design,' the lack of any defense-in-depth KZG check at the CL level means the VerifiedRODataColumn type invariant is violated.
phase3_5.recommendation: Either (a) perform KZG proof verification on reconstructed EL data before wrapping as VerifiedRODataColumn, or (b) introduce a separate type ELReconstructedRODataColumn that does not carry the 'verified' semantic guarantee, to prevent it from being inadvertently passed to code paths that assume full cryptographic verification.
phase3_5.severity_estimate: Medium - requires EL compromise, but the cryptographic verification gap is architecturally significant for a consensus-critical system

audit_items.final_reasoning: The ReconstructDataColumnSidecars function marks EL-provided data as VerifiedRODataColumn without performing any KZG proof verification, violating the documented invariant of that type ('should only be used by the verification package'). While the EL is trusted by design, this creates a systemic architectural risk where a compromised or buggy EL can silently inject malformed data columns that are stored and broadcast as cryptographically verified. This is a design-level trust boundary violation with Medium severity.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Does the node enforce subscription checks before publishing data column sidecars?

audit_items.state_context: allDataColumnSubnets returns all subnets when validators tracked (custody > 0). This is used for peer subscription management, NOT for broadcast gating. Callers (broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars, proposer, subscriber) all correctly compute subnet via peerdas.ComputeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar. The custody check is entirely caller-side responsibility.

phase1.summary: BroadcastDataColumnSidecar in broadcaster.go accepts a subnet index parameter and unconditionally constructs the gossipsub topic for that subnet, then dispatches internalBroadcastDataColumnSidecar. The internal function calls findPeersIfNeeded to discover peers for the given subnet (finding and dialing peers even for non-custodied subnets), then broadcastObject. There is no check anywhere in this call chain that the node custodies the given subnet.
state_anomalies: A node can broadcast on any subnet regardless of whether it custodies that subnet
findPeersIfNeeded will actively discover and connect to peers for non-custodied subnets to fulfill the broadcast, expanding the node's connection set unnecessarily
The API provides no protection against callers passing incorrect subnets
phase1.cache_analysis: No relevant caching. The broadcast is fire-and-forget.
phase1.concurrency_analysis: Broadcast is non-blocking (goroutine dispatch). Multiple concurrent broadcasts for different subnets can happen simultaneously, which is by design and does not cause race conditions.

phase2.summary: Primary scenario: a node with no custody requirement calls BroadcastDataColumnSidecar for any subnet - the broadcast proceeds unconditionally. However, all current callers correctly compute the subnet from the column index and only broadcast for custodied columns: broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars only broadcasts missing custody columns; the proposer path only broadcasts for self-built block columns.
phase2.counterexample: Partial - in broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars, a node broadcasts reconstructed data columns for its custody columns. Since these ARE custody columns, the lack of a custody check in BroadcastDataColumnSidecar does not cause incorrect behavior in that path. The concern is API contract: any caller can pass any subnet and the function will broadcast without checking custody.
attack_scenarios: A future developer calls BroadcastDataColumnSidecar(root, wrongSubnet, sidecar) by mistake - the function broadcasts to the wrong subnet with no error indication
A validator proposer node broadcasts data columns to subnets it does not custody, violating Fulu spec 'a node MUST NOT gossip sidecars for columns it does not custody'

phase2_5.reachability: This function is called from three locations: broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars (correct subnet), subscriber_beacon_blocks.go (correct subnet), and proposer.go (correct subnet). All callers correctly compute the subnet via peerdas.ComputeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar. The API-level gap is not currently exploited by existing callers.
entry_points: Internal call from reconstruction, subscription, and proposer code paths
phase2_5.classification: internal-only (currently). The gap is a missing API-level safeguard, not an active vulnerability with current callers.

phase3.summary: The Fulu spec states that nodes should only broadcast data column sidecars on subnets they custody. The BroadcastDataColumnSidecar API does not enforce this invariant. The specification requires that 'a node MUST NOT gossip sidecars for columns it does not custody.' Currently, all callers happen to compute the correct subnet and only broadcast for custodied columns, so the invariant holds in practice, but the guard is absent at the API level.
phase3.guard_identified: None in BroadcastDataColumnSidecar. Callers are responsible for subnet correctness.
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Insufficient as an API contract; sufficient for current call sites only.
edge_cases: Node with custodyGroupCount=0 (non-custodying node) could theoretically call this
Future code paths that pass computed subnets could introduce bugs without a custody check in the broadcaster

phase3_5.reason: The absence of a custody check in BroadcastDataColumnSidecar violates the Fulu spec requirement that nodes only broadcast on custodied subnets. While current callers are correct, the API provides no protection against future or accidental misuse, creating a spec compliance gap.
phase3_5.recommendation: Add a custody check at the beginning of BroadcastDataColumnSidecar (or in internalBroadcastDataColumnSidecar) that verifies the node custodies the given dataColumnSubnet before proceeding. Return an error or log a warning if broadcasting on a non-custodied subnet.
phase3_5.severity_estimate: Low - no current exploitable path, but a spec compliance gap that could cause incorrect behavior if call sites evolve

audit_items.final_reasoning: BroadcastDataColumnSidecar does not enforce a custody check before broadcasting, violating the Fulu spec requirement. However, all current callers correctly compute and pass custodied subnets, so there is no active exploit path. The gap is a missing API-level safeguard and a spec compliance issue that could become exploitable if future code paths are less careful about subnet computation.

checklist_item.title: Can the anti-equivocation cache update be bypassed when sidecar publishing is skipped?

audit_items.state_context: seenDataColumnCache is used as anti-equivocation mechanism. reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars saves toSaveSidecars (custody only) then schedules broadcast via time.AfterFunc (1-3 second delay). setSeenDataColumnIndex is NOT called during save - deferred to broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars. The code comment explains: 'We do not call receiveDataColumn, because it will ignore incoming data columns via gossip while we did not broadcast (yet) the reconstructed data columns.'

phase1.summary: The seenDataColumnCache serves as an anti-equivocation mechanism: once a column is marked 'seen,' validateDataColumn returns pubsub.ValidationIgnore for that (slot, proposerIndex, index) triple. In broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars, the sequence is: (1) check hasSeenDataColumnIndex, (2) if not seen, load from storage, (3) call BroadcastDataColumnSidecar, (4) call setSeenDataColumnIndex. In receiveDataColumnSidecar (gossip path), the sequence is: (1) call setSeenDataColumnIndex, then (2) process. In reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars, sidecars are saved via dataColumnStorage.Save bypassing receiveDataColumnSidecar, and setSeenDataColumnIndex is NOT called here.
state_anomalies: Between Save(toSaveSidecars) and eventual call to broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars (1-3 second delay via time.AfterFunc), reconstructed sidecars are in storage but NOT marked as seen in seenDataColumnCache

TOCTOU race: between hasSeenDataColumnIndex check and BroadcastDataColumnSidecar call, a concurrent gossip handler may mark the same index as seen, causing the sidecar to be broadcast even after it arrived via gossip
setSeenDataColumnIndex is called AFTER BroadcastDataColumnSidecar in broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars but BEFORE processing in receiveDataColumnSidecar - inconsistent ordering
phase1.cache_analysis: seenDataColumnCache is a slotAwareCache with individually thread-safe operations (setSeenDataColumnIndex and hasSeenDataColumnIndex), but the combined check-then-broadcast in broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars is not atomic.
phase1.concurrency_analysis: reconstructionLock prevents concurrent reconstructions during save. However, the lock is released before scheduleMissingDataColumnSidecarsBroadcast is called. The broadcast happens in a time.AfterFunc callback outside the lock, creating a window for concurrent gossip handler execution.

phase2.summary: TOCTOU scenario: (1) Reconstruction completes, sidecars saved, broadcast scheduled for T+1.5s. (2) At T+0.5s, same sidecar arrives via gossip, passes validation, setSeenDataColumnIndex is called. (3) At T+1.5s, broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars runs, checks hasSeenDataColumnIndex - returns true - correctly skips broadcast. This path works correctly. Inverted scenario: (1) broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars runs, calls hasSeenDataColumnIndex - returns false. (2) Concurrently, gossip handler marks it as seen. (3) BroadcastDataColumnSidecar is called anyway. Result: duplicate broadcast.
phase2.counterexample: The TOCTOU produces duplicate broadcasts but not a safety failure. The anti-equivocation cache is not 'bypassed' in the security sense - it does not allow an invalid sidecar to pass or prevent a valid sidecar from being processed. The concern in the check description appears to refer to the intentional window where sidecars are not yet marked seen after reconstruction.
attack_scenarios: TOCTOU race causes duplicate broadcast of a sidecar that was already received via gossip (extra network message, not safety violation)
An external peer timing their gossip message to the reconstruction broadcast window cannot cause any security failure
phase2.timing_dependencies: Yes - requires concurrent gossip arrival during the 1-3 second broadcast delay window

phase2_5.reachability: The TOCTOU is reachable through concurrent execution of the gossip handler and the scheduled broadcast timer. A peer that sends a gossip sidecar in the precise window after reconstruction completes and before the broadcast fires can influence timing. However, the outcome is only a duplicate broadcast, not a security failure.
entry_points: Internal timer callback (time.AfterFunc) + gossip handler concurrency
phase2_5.classification: defense-in-depth (timing-dependent, limited impact - duplicate broadcasts only)

phase3.summary: Invariant to prove: 'After reconstruction, no sidecar is broadcast that was already received via gossip.' This invariant holds probabilistically (the deferred setSeenDataColumnIndex in broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars provides a check), but has a TOCTOU gap. The invariant 'a sidecar received via gossip is processed exactly once' holds correctly because the gossip path marks seen before processing. The invariant 'a reconstructed sidecar is not broadcast if it has already been received via gossip' holds most of the time but not always due to the race.
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Insufficient - not atomic with subsequent broadcast call
edge_cases: High-latency gossip where the sidecar arrives exactly at the broadcast window
Multiple concurrent reconstructions blocked by reconstructionLock that then fire broadcasts sequentially

phase3_5.reason: The TOCTOU race in the anti-equivocation check (hasSeenDataColumnIndex check not atomic with BroadcastDataColumnSidecar call) represents a correctness gap that can cause duplicate broadcasts. The intentional design of deferring setSeenDataColumnIndex until after broadcast creates a deliberate window of inconsistency. Impact is limited to extra network traffic, not a safety failure.
phase3_5.recommendation: In broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars, use setSeenDataColumnIndex as a compare-and-swap (returning whether the set was a new entry) to atomically mark-then-broadcast, preventing duplicate broadcasts in the TOCTOU window.
phase3_5.severity_estimate: Low - impact is extra broadcast traffic (network noise), not a security violation

audit_items.final_reasoning: The TOCTOU race between the hasSeenDataColumnIndex check and the BroadcastDataColumnSidecar call in broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars can cause duplicate broadcasts during the reconstruction window. This is a correctness gap but not a security failure. The intentional design (deferring seen marking to allow gossip-received duplicates to be processed during reconstruction) is correct but creates a non-atomic check-then-act sequence. Impact: extra network traffic only.

checklist_item.title: Can imported data columns bypass gossip validation rules?

audit_items.state_context: gossip validateDataColumn applies full validation including KZG proof verification via validateWithKzgBatchVerifier. Reconstructed sidecars are broadcast directly via BroadcastDataColumnSidecar which goes to broadcastObject (gossipsub publish) without re-running validateDataColumn. Receiving peers will apply full validation when they receive the broadcast. peerdas.ReconstructDataColumnSidecars operates on VerifiedRODataColumn inputs that previously passed gossip validation including SidecarKzgProofVerified.

phase1.summary: reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars reconstructs data columns from storage-resident, already-verified sidecars via peerdas.ReconstructDataColumnSidecars. The reconstruction function operates on VerifiedRODataColumn inputs (which were previously gossip-validated including KZG proof verification) and produces new VerifiedRODataColumn outputs. These reconstructed outputs are then saved via dataColumnStorage.Save (bypassing receiveDataColumnSidecar) and subsequently broadcast via BroadcastDataColumnSidecar (bypassing validateDataColumn). The gossip validation rules skipped include: ValidFields, CorrectSubnet, NotFromFutureSlot, SidecarParentSeen, SidecarParentValid, ValidProposerSignature, SidecarParentSlotLower, SidecarDescendsFromFinalized, SidecarInclusionProven, SidecarKzgProofVerified, SidecarProposerExpected.
state_anomalies: SidecarKzgProofVerified is not applied to reconstructed sidecars - KZG cell proofs for reconstructed columns are generated by the reconstruction algorithm but not explicitly re-verified

SidecarProposerExpected is skipped - verifies proposer index against expected shuffling; a reconstructed sidecar with a valid signature but wrong proposer index would pass reconstruction and be broadcast
ValidFields is skipped - structural nil checks; reconstructed sidecars inherit block header from input sidecars so structurally valid
ValidProposerSignature is skipped - signed block header is copied from input sidecars with same valid signature
phase1.cache_analysis: Reconstructed sidecars are saved to storage and served to peers via RPC. If the reconstruction algorithm produces incorrect KZG proofs (due to corrupt inputs), those incorrect proofs would be served to and rejected by peers who validate them via gossip or RPC verification.
phase1.concurrency_analysis: reconstructionLock prevents concurrent reconstructions. Scheduled broadcast is outside the lock via time.AfterFunc callback.

phase2.summary: Tracing the KZG proof skip: peerdas.ReconstructDataColumnSidecars takes verified input sidecars, performs Reed-Solomon recovery to reconstruct missing cells, computes new KZG cell proofs, and wraps them as VerifiedRODataColumn. The reconstruction is based on KZG principles where if the input is correct, the reconstruction is cryptographically correct by the properties of the Reed-Solomon code. If the minimum threshold (>=64 of 128 columns) of valid input columns is met and all inputs have valid KZG proofs (which they do, having passed gossip validation), the reconstructed outputs are mathematically guaranteed to have correct KZG proofs.
phase2.counterexample: No direct counterexample for the happy path (valid input -> valid reconstruction). Theoretical concern: if any prior step in the gossip pipeline accepted a sidecar with an invalid KZG proof (e.g., via a bug in the batch KZG verifier or a race condition in verification), that sidecar could be used as reconstruction input, producing incorrect outputs broadcast as verified. The SidecarProposerExpected skip is a more concrete gap: receiving peers will reject incorrectly-proposer-indexed reconstructed sidecars, but the node itself broadcasts and stores them without verifying this property.
attack_scenarios: If an attacker can inject a gossip sidecar that passes all validation except KZG (via a bug in the batch verifier), and that sidecar is stored and used as reconstruction input, the reconstructed outputs would be incorrect but broadcast as verified
Equivocating proposer sending two valid signed block headers for the same slot: reconstructed sidecars inherit the header but the node stores data without SidecarProposerExpected check
phase2.timing_dependencies: None - reconstruction is triggered by gossip sidecar arrival

phase2_5.reachability: Reconstructed sidecars are broadcast to peers via gossip. When peers receive them, they run the full validateDataColumn pipeline including all the checks that were skipped during reconstruction. So the 'bypassed' validations are effectively re-applied by the recipient's gossip validator. This means the bypass is local to the node's storage and broadcast pipeline.
phase2_5.classification: defense-in-depth. The skipped validations are re-enforced by receiving peers. An external attacker who supplies the minimum valid set of gossip sidecars can trigger reconstruction of the missing columns, but the reconstructed outputs are mathematically correct (from valid inputs) and will pass peer validation.

phase3.summary: Invariant to prove: 'Reconstructed sidecars that are broadcast satisfy all gossip validation rules that a receiving peer would apply.' Analysis of each skipped check: (1) ValidFields - Satisfied, inherited from valid input. (2) CorrectSubnet - Satisfied, caller computes correctly via ComputeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar. (3) NotFromFutureSlot - Satisfied, inherited slot from valid input. (4) SidecarParentSeen/Valid - Satisfied, block was already processed. (5) ValidProposerSignature - Satisfied, same signed block header as input. (6) SidecarParentSlotLower/SidecarDescendsFromFinalized - Satisfied, same block ancestry. (7) SidecarInclusionProven - Satisfied, same KZG commitments inclusion proof. (8) SidecarKzgProofVerified - Conditionally satisfied if reconstruction is mathematically correct from valid inputs (Reed-Solomon guarantee). (9) SidecarProposerExpected - NOT verified locally; receiving peers will apply this check.
phase3.guard_identified: The gossip validation pipeline that verified the input sidecars serves as the implicit guard for the reconstruction's correctness. Receiving peers re-apply all gossip validation rules.
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient under the assumption that the batch KZG verifier is correct and no prior validation bypass occurred. The Reed-Solomon mathematical guarantee ensures that reconstructed outputs from valid inputs have correct KZG proofs.
edge_cases: If the batch KZG verifier has a false-accept bug, it could be exploited to inject bad data into reconstruction inputs
SidecarProposerExpected is not locally verified - receiving peers will reject incorrectly-proposer-indexed sidecars, but the node stores and broadcasts them
If blobsAndProofs.KzgProofs has wrong count per blob, ConstructDataColumnSidecars may produce structurally invalid sidecars that receiving peers reject

phase3_5.reason: While the bypass of gossip validation rules during reconstruction is largely justified by mathematical guarantees of Reed-Solomon reconstruction from cryptographically-verified inputs, the explicit skipping of SidecarKzgProofVerified and SidecarProposerExpected creates a dependency on prior validation pipeline correctness. The code comment explicitly acknowledges the bypass ('We do not call receiveDataColumn'). The SidecarProposerExpected skip is worth specifically flagging: the node stores and broadcasts reconstructed sidecars without verifying the proposer index matches expected shuffling, relying entirely on receiving peers to catch this.
phase3_5.recommendation: Add an explicit KZG proof verification step on reconstructed sidecars before wrapping them as VerifiedRODataColumn, even if deferred/background to avoid impacting reconstruction latency. For SidecarProposerExpected, consider adding a local check before broadcasting reconstructed sidecars to avoid broadcasting data that receiving peers will reject.
phase3_5.severity_estimate: Low to Medium - practical risk is low given defense-in-depth from receiving peers re-validating, but the architectural gap (propagating data without full verification) is noteworthy in a consensus-critical system

audit_items.final_reasoning: Reconstructed data column sidecars bypass the full gossip validation pipeline (validateDataColumn) before being stored and broadcast. While most validation invariants are preserved by mathematical properties of Reed-Solomon reconstruction from verified inputs, the explicit bypass of SidecarKzgProofVerified and SidecarProposerExpected creates a dependency on prior validation pipeline correctness. Receiving peers provide the defense-in-depth by re-validating all gossip messages. This is a design-level validation bypass that is architecturally significant for a consensus-critical system, even with the indirect mitigation.
